svg.title: Proof. Fix a site z and conjugate by wi = eb dist(z,li). The conjugated entry is Bijwi/wj and |wi/wj −1| ≤b dijeb dij with dij = dist(li, lj), by the triangle inequality and |et −1| ≤|t|e|t|. For b ≤a/4, b d ebde−ad ≤b(4/a)e−(a/2)d because d e−(a/4)d ≤4/(ea) ≤4/a. The perturbation therefore has row and column sums at most Cb(4/a)Kc(a/2) ≤M/2, hence quadratic-form price at most M/2, and the conjugated matrix eB has counting coercivity M/2. Solve Bu = ej, take z = lj and vi = wiui; then eBv = ej since wj = 1, and coercivity gives (M/2) P i v2 i ≤vj. Thus (M/2)v2 j ≤vj, vj ≤2/M, and then v2 i ≤(2/M)vj ≤(2/M)2. Undoing the weight gives the entry bound and summing a row gives the norm bound. Only the counting gap and exponential summability are used; no equivalence of maximum and Euclidean norms enters.
